executable_actions.on_failure: Keep SACG extraction blocked. Record each failed or not-run checker against its affected constraint and source artifact, retain the prepared-input error as unresolved if it remains unclassified, and route only checker-grounded violations to their bounded owners. Do not infer a pass from absent detail or make unapproved design changes.
executable_actions.rationale: The available summaries do not establish specialist outcomes or classify the prepared-input error. Aggregate the named audits with their source constraints, run the registered checks, and emit an evidence-linked readiness decision rather than assuming missing detail is a missing artifact or a pass.

observations: The state summary identifies the design, model, numeric, template, board, tool, and human-boundary inputs, but it does not provide their detailed values or checker results.

The candidate artifact summary is compact and reports additional output keys beyond those shown. The four specialist audit artifacts are expected by the role assignment, but their detailed contents and statuses are not inspectable here; this is not evidence that they are missing.
prepared_inputs.errors contains one item, but its content and specialist classification are not supplied. Retain it as an unresolved blocker until classified against evidence.
No registered checker outcomes are supplied, so readiness and any individual constraint pass cannot be claimed.
sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers, open retry requests, and open backtrack requests. None is a current SACG-memory blocker.
No validated lower-layer certificates are supplied. They are not required to establish input-preparation readiness and must not be represented as current-scope evidence.

The applicable verification acceptance policy is current-source real VCS compilation, elaboration, and linking. Runtime simulation, golden comparisons, waveform evidence, and weight loading are not additional acceptance prerequisites.
proposed_actions: Aggregate the four specialist audits with the source inputs, run the registered cross-layer and boundary checkers, and produce the three required readiness/gap/boundary artifacts with evidence bound to SACG constraints.

Classify the existing prepared-input error from the audit and checker evidence. If it is still unresolved, keep SACG extraction blocked and route only the demonstrated violation to its bounded repair owner.
Do not alter templates, architecture, memory layout, numeric policy, golden/reference data, or board interfaces as part of this audit.
risks: Model identity/decoder and model-shape alignment with the task card cannot be assessed from the supplied summaries.
Numeric policy, tolerance provenance, template coverage, and parameter binding cannot be cross-checked without audit details and checker outcomes.
Architecture and data/stream order consistency with board memory and runtime constraints remains unverified.
Tool protocol and evidence provenance are unverified; do not equate configured tool availability or planned checks with successful tool evidence.
Human approval and forbidden-action boundaries are not visible in sufficient detail to confirm the proposed repair scope.
The unclassified prepared-input error could affect any of these constraint groups; assigning it to a repair owner before evidence-based classification would be speculative.
